arguments.name: defaultVersion
arguments.description: (Optional) Default Version of the launch template.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) Description of the launch template.

arguments.name: disableApiStop
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, enables [EC2 Instance Stop Protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-stop-protection.html).

arguments.name: disableApiTermination
arguments.description: (Optional) If `true`, enables [EC2 Instance Termination Protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_ChangingDisableAPITermination.html)

arguments.name: ebsOptimized
arguments.description: (Optional) If `true`, the launched EC2 instance will be EBS-optimized.

arguments.name: imageId
arguments.description: (Optional) The AMI from which to launch the instance or use a Systems Manager parameter convention e.g. `resolve:ssm:parameter-name`. See [docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/create-launch-template.html#use-an-ssm-parameter-instead-of-an-ami-id) for more details.

arguments.name: instanceInitiatedShutdownBehavior
arguments.description: (Optional) Shutdown behavior for the instance. Can be `stop` or `terminate`.

arguments.name: instanceType
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of the instance. If present then `instanceRequirements` cannot be present.

arguments.name: kernelId
arguments.description: (Optional) The kernel ID.

arguments.name: keyName
arguments.description: (Optional) The key name to use for the instance.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the launch template. If you leave this blank, Terraform will auto-generate a unique name.

arguments.name: namePrefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.

arguments.name: ramDiskId
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the RAM disk.

arguments.name: securityGroupNames
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group names to associate with. If you are creating Instances in a VPC, use `vpcSecurityGroupIds` instead.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the launch template. If configured with a provider [`defaultTags` configuration block](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#default_tags-configuration-block) present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.

arguments.name: updateDefaultVersion
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to update Default Version each update. Conflicts with `defaultVersion`.

arguments.name: userData
arguments.description: (Optional) The base64-encoded user data to provide when launching the instance.

arguments.name: vpcSecurityGroupIds
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group IDs to associate with. Conflicts with `network_interfaces.security_groups`

arguments.name: deviceName
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the device to mount.

arguments.name: noDevice
arguments.description: (Optional) Suppresses the specified device included in the AMI's block device mapping.

arguments.name: virtualName
arguments.description: (Optional) The [Instance Store Device Name](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html#InstanceStoreDeviceNames) (e.g., `"ephemeral0"`).

arguments.name: deleteOnTermination
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the volume should be destroyed on instance termination.

arguments.name: encrypted
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables [EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html) on the volume.

arguments.name: iops
arguments.description: (Optional) The amount of provisioned [IOPS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-io-characteristics.html).

arguments.name: kmsKeyId
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer master key (CMK) to use when creating the encrypted volume.

arguments.name: snapshotId
arguments.description: (Optional) The Snapshot ID to mount.

arguments.name: throughput
arguments.description: (Optional) The throughput to provision for a `gp3` volume in MiB/s (specified as an integer, e.g., 500), with a maximum of 1,000 MiB/s.

arguments.name: volumeInitializationRate
arguments.description: (Optional) The volume initialization rate in MiB/s (specified as an integer, e.g. 100), with a minimum of 100 MiB/s and maximum of 300 MiB/s.

arguments.name: volumeSize
arguments.description: (Optional) The size of the volume in gigabytes.

arguments.name: volumeType
arguments.description: (Optional) The volume type.

arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator manufacturer names. Default is any manufacturer.

arguments.name: acceleratorNames
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator names. Default is any acclerator.

arguments.name: acceleratorTypes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator types. Default is any accelerator type.

arguments.name: allowedInstanceTypes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of instance types to apply your specified attributes against. All other instance types are ignored, even if they match your specified attributes. You can use strings with one or more wild cards, represented by an asterisk (\*), to allow an instance type, size, or generation. The following are examples: `m5.8xlarge`, `c5*.*`, `m5a.*`, `r*`, `*3*`. For example, if you specify `c5*`, you are allowing the entire C5 instance family, which includes all C5a and C5n instance types. If you specify `m5a.*`, you are allowing all the M5a instance types, but not the M5n instance types. Maximum of 400 entries in the list; each entry is limited to 30 characters. Default is all instance types.

arguments.name: bareMetal
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether bare metal instace types should be `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `excluded`.

arguments.name: burstablePerformance
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether burstable performance instance types should be `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `excluded`.

arguments.name: excludedInstanceTypes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of instance types to exclude. You can use strings with one or more wild cards, represented by an asterisk (\*), to exclude an instance type, size, or generation. The following are examples: `m5.8xlarge`, `c5*.*`, `m5a.*`, `r*`, `*3*`. For example, if you specify `c5*`, you are excluding the entire C5 instance family, which includes all C5a and C5n instance types. If you specify `m5a.*`, you are excluding all the M5a instance types, but not the M5n instance types. Maximum of 400 entries in the list; each entry is limited to 30 characters. Default is no excluded instance types.

arguments.name: instanceGenerations
arguments.description: (Optional) List of instance generation names. Default is any generation.

arguments.name: localStorage
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether instance types with local storage volumes are `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `included`.

arguments.name: localStorageTypes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of local storage type names. Default any storage type.

arguments.name: maxSpotPriceAsPercentageOfOptimalOnDemandPrice
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for Spot Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for a Spot Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Conflicts with `spotMaxPricePercentageOverLowestPrice`

arguments.name: onDemandMaxPricePercentageOverLowestPrice
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for On-Demand Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for an On-Demand Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Default is 20.

arguments.name: requireHibernateSupport
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether instance types must support On-Demand Instance Hibernation, either `true` or `false`. Default is `false`.

arguments.name: spotMaxPricePercentageOverLowestPrice
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for Spot Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for a Spot Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Default is 100. Conflicts with `maxSpotPriceAsPercentageOfOptimalOnDemandPrice` If you set DesiredCapacityType to vcpu or memory-mib, the price protection threshold is applied based on the per vCPU or per memory price instead of the per instance price.

arguments.name: autoRecovery
arguments.description: (Optional) Disables the automatic recovery behavior of your instance or sets it to default. Can be `"default"` or `"disabled"`. See [Recover your instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-recover.html) for more details.

arguments.name: httpEndpoint
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the metadata service is available. Can be `"enabled"` or `"disabled"`. (Default: `"enabled"`).

arguments.name: httpProtocolIpv6
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the IPv6 endpoint for the instance metadata service. Can be `"enabled"` or `"disabled"`.

arguments.name: httpPutResponseHopLimit
arguments.description: (Optional) The desired HTTP PUT response hop limit for instance metadata requests. The larger the number, the further instance metadata requests can travel. Can be an integer from `1` to `64`. (Default: `1`).

arguments.name: httpTokens
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether or not the metadata service requires session tokens, also referred to as _Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2)_. Can be `"optional"` or `"required"`. (Default: `"optional"`).

arguments.name: instanceMetadataTags
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables access to instance tags from the instance metadata service. Can be `"enabled"` or `"disabled"`.

arguments.name: associateCarrierIpAddress
arguments.description: (Optional) Associate a Carrier IP address with `eth0` for a new network interface. Use this option when you launch an instance in a Wavelength Zone and want to associate a Carrier IP address with the network interface. Boolean value, can be left unset.

arguments.name: associatePublicIpAddress
arguments.description: (Optional) Associate a public ip address with the network interface. Boolean value, can be left unset.

arguments.name: deleteOnTermination
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the network interface should be destroyed on instance termination.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) Description of the network interface.

arguments.name: deviceIndex
arguments.description: (Optional) The integer index of the network interface attachment.

arguments.name: interfaceType
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of network interface. To create an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), specify `efa`.

arguments.name: ipv4AddressCount
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to assign to a network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4Addresses`

arguments.name: ipv4Addresses
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more private IPv4 addresses to associate. Conflicts with `ipv4AddressCount`

arguments.name: ipv4PrefixCount
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv4 prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4Prefixes`

arguments.name: ipv4Prefixes
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more IPv4 prefixes to be assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv4PrefixCount`

arguments.name: ipv6AddressCount
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv6 addresses to assign to a network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6Addresses`

arguments.name: ipv6Addresses
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more specific IPv6 addresses from the IPv6 CIDR block range of your subnet. Conflicts with `ipv6AddressCount`

arguments.name: ipv6PrefixCount
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of IPv6 prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6Prefixes`

arguments.name: ipv6Prefixes
arguments.description: (Optional) One or more IPv6 prefixes to be assigned to the network interface. Conflicts with `ipv6PrefixCount`

arguments.name: networkCardIndex
arguments.description: (Optional) The index of the network card. Some instance types support multiple network cards. The primary network interface must be assigned to network card index 0. The default is network card index 0.

arguments.name: networkInterfaceId
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the network interface to attach.

arguments.name: primaryIpv6
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the first IPv6 GUA will be made the primary IPv6 address.

arguments.name: privateIpAddress
arguments.description: (Optional) The primary private IPv4 address.

arguments.name: securityGroups
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group IDs to associate.

arguments.name: subnetId
arguments.description: (Optional) The VPC Subnet ID to associate.

arguments.name: tcpEstablishedTimeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle TCP connections in an established state. Min: 60 seconds. Max: 432000 seconds (5 days). Default: 432000 seconds. Recommended: Less than 432000 seconds.

arguments.name: udpStreamTimeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle UDP flows that have seen traffic only in a single direction or a single request-response transaction. Min: 30 seconds. Max: 60 seconds. Default: 30 seconds.

arguments.name: udpTimeout
arguments.description: (Optional) Timeout (in seconds) for idle UDP flows classified as streams which have seen more than one request-response transaction. Min: 60 seconds. Max: 180 seconds (3 minutes). Default: 180 seconds.

arguments.name: enaSrdEnabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable ENA Express. ENA Express uses AWS Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) technology to improve the performance of TCP traffic.

arguments.name: enaSrdUdpEnabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to enable UDP traffic optimization through ENA Express. Requires `enaSrdEnabled` to be `true`.

arguments.name: affinity
arguments.description: (Optional) The affinity setting for an instance on a Dedicated Host.

arguments.name: availabilityZone
arguments.description: (Optional) The Availability Zone for the instance.

arguments.name: groupName
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the placement group for the instance.

arguments.name: hostId
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the Dedicated Host for the instance.

arguments.name: hostResourceGroupArn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the Host Resource Group in which to launch instances.

arguments.name: partitionNumber
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of the partition the instance should launch in. Valid only if the placement group strategy is set to partition.

arguments.name: spreadDomain
arguments.description: (Optional) Reserved for future use.

arguments.name: tenancy
arguments.description: (Optional) The tenancy of the instance (if the instance is running in a VPC). Can be `default`, `dedicated`, or `host`.

arguments.name: enableResourceNameDnsARecord
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to respond to DNS queries for instance hostnames with DNS A records.

arguments.name: enableResourceNameDnsAaaaRecord
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to respond to DNS queries for instance hostnames with DNS AAAA records.

arguments.name: hostnameType
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of hostname for Amazon EC2 instances. For IPv4 only subnets, an instance DNS name must be based on the instance IPv4 address. For IPv6 native subnets, an instance DNS name must be based on the instance ID. For dual-stack subnets, you can specify whether DNS names use the instance IPv4 address or the instance ID. Valid values: `ip-name` and `resource-name`.

arguments.name: resourceType
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of resource to tag.

arguments.description: (Optional)  A map of tags to assign to the resource.
